# Supported variable and tag reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_reference.py. Do not edit by hand: change the role defaults,
     the role tasks or docs/reference-annotations.yml, then run `make reference`. -->

This is the public configuration surface of the `curiosity.workstation` collection: every role variable with its type, default, valid values, stability and safety impact, the tags a focused run can select, and the profile selectors. It is generated from the role defaults and tasks; CI fails when it is out of date (`make reference-check`). [configuration.md](configuration.md) explains the options in prose.

## How to read this reference

Stability:

- **supported**: Part of the public configuration API. Changes follow the deprecation policy.
- **experimental**: Works today but may change or be removed without a deprecation period.
- **internal**: Implementation detail (derived value, file path or contract table). Do not set it; it may change in any release.
- **private-hook**: Integration point for a private service or organisation. The collection ships it empty; the value belongs in protected host variables, not in a public repository.

Variables not marked otherwise are **supported**. The marking is curated in [reference-annotations.yml](reference-annotations.yml); a variable missing from it is supported by default, so review new variables when they are added.

Safety impact (a variable can carry several flags; blank means no special concern):

- **secret**: Credential, token or key. Keep it in protected host variables or a vault, never in git.
- **destructive**: Can erase, repartition or reformat data.
- **security**: Changes the host's security posture (firewall, SSH, integrity checks, certificate trust).
- **network**: Changes networking, DNS or VPN routing. A wrong value can cut off remote access.
- **boot**: Changes boot, console or display configuration. A wrong value can leave the host without a usable display.
- **supply-chain**: Downloads and installs software from a configured location. Pin it with the matching checksum or fingerprint.
- **account**: Creates, changes or grants access to user accounts.

Defaults of dictionaries and long values are summarised here; read the role's `defaults/main.yml` for the full value.

## Profiles

Two independent selectors choose what a host converges. Any `workstation_profile` can be combined with any hardware profile.

- `workstation_profile` (default `"desktop"`):
  - `desktop`: full workstation (physical/VM desktop host)
  - `workspace`: container-safe Coder workspace profile
  - `thin-client`: access appliance for Coder + Ziti + browser
  - `byod-kiosk`: Locked-down full-screen browser session (see kiosk_target_url and the kiosk and lockdown tags).
- `hardware_profile` (default `"generic"`): `generic`, `arm-thin-client`, `x86-byod-laptop`, `z590`, `deskmeet-b760`, `t460`.

Settings each hardware profile defines in `hardware_profiles` (names only):

| Hardware profile | Description | Settings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `generic` | Generic developer workstation (no hardware-specific drivers) | `packages`, `services`, `pia_vpn` |
| `arm-thin-client` | ARM thin client | `packages`, `services`, `pia_vpn` |
| `x86-byod-laptop` | x86_64 BYOD laptop (Lenovo T460 and similar) | `packages`, `disable_sleep`, `performance_mode`, `services`, `pia_vpn`, `console_diagnostics` |
| `z590` | ASUS TUF Gaming Z590 — iGPU passthrough VM host | `packages`, `services`, `pipx_packages`, `udev_rules`, `pia_vpn` |
| `deskmeet-b760` | ASRock DeskMeet B760 — Intel Arc A380 + desk USB hub peripherals | `hhtest_host`, `hhtest_authorized_keys`, `firewall`, `firewall_ssh_interfaces`, `firewall_mosh`, `untrusted_lan`, `dns_over_tls_interfaces`, `packages`, `services`, `disable_sleep`, `performance_mode`, `litra_cli`, `logitech_g604`, `samsung_tv_cli`, `streamstack`, `double_click_ms`, `idle_lock_minutes`, `i915_pcon_frl_444`, `display_outputs`, `console_video`, `display_guard`, `console_tuning`, `broadcast_rgb`, `display_scale`, `compositor_enabled`, `greeter`, `xorg_accel_method`, `xorg_auto_add_gpu`, `xorg_gdb_trace`, `xorg_preferred_modes`, `pointer_accel_speed`, `pipx_packages`, `udev_rules`, `modprobe_options`, `kernel_modules`, `pia_vpn` |
| `t460` | Lenovo ThinkPad T460/T560— Intel HD 520 (Skylake GT2) + Validity VFS5011 fingerprint | `packages`, `disable_sleep`, `performance_mode`, `services`, `pipx_packages`, `udev_rules`, `pia_vpn`, `console_diagnostics` |

| Variable | Type | Default | Valid values | Status | Safety impact | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dev_user` | string | `"curiosity"` |  | supported | account | (undocumented) |
| `dev_user_home` | string | `"/home/curiosity"` |  | supported |  | (undocumented) |
| `dev_users` | list | `[{"name": "{{ dev_user }}", "home": "{{ dev_user_home }}"}]` |  | supported | account | Interactive accounts that receive per-user desktop and systemd convergence. `dev_user` stays the primary account for every other user-scoped task and must be listed here. (...) |
| `workstation_user_linger` | list | `[]` |  | supported |  | Accounts whose systemd user manager must keep running without a login session (`loginctl enable-linger`). Empty leaves lingering untouched. |
| `earlyoom_mem_percent` | string | `"5"` | integer percent, 1 to 100, written as a string | supported |  | earlyoom thresholds (percent of available memory / free swap). earlyoom acts only when BOTH memory and swap are below their limits. Defaults keep the historical 5% memory and 50% swap behavior (SIGKILL at half of each). |
| `earlyoom_swap_percent` | string | `"50"` | integer percent, 1 to 100, written as a string | supported |  | (undocumented) |
| `earlyoom_prefer_regex` | string | `""` |  | supported |  | Optional process-name regexes (matched against the kernel comm name, 15 chars). Empty adds no --prefer / --avoid flag. Hosts that run long-lived agent sessions set these so browsers die before the agents do. |
| `earlyoom_avoid_regex` | string | `""` |  | supported |  | (undocumented) |
| `workstation_timezone` | string | `""` |  | supported |  | IANA time zone for the system clock (`timedatectl`), e.g. America/New_York. Empty leaves the host's zone untouched. StreamStack's light schedule takes its sunrise and sunset from this zone unless streamstack_latitude/longitude are set. |
| `developer_workstation_local_vars_file` | string | `"/etc/ansible/local-vars.yml"` |  | supported |  | Optional machine-local override file. Keep per-person/user values here on the target host instead of committing host-specific maps to this repo. |

This is intentionally empty for the public baseline: site operators can declare obsolete or superseded user timers in protected inventory without putting private application names in the collection. (...) |
